apps.name: Helix
apps.text: A modal text editor with multiple selections and syntax trees built in.

apps.name: micro
apps.text: A terminal text editor with the keys people already know: Ctrl-S saves, Ctrl-Q quits.

apps.name: Kakoune
apps.text: A modal editor where you select first and act second. Runs shell snippets, so it may run other programs.

apps.name: Vim
apps.text: The classic modal editor, with its full runtime of syntax files and plugins.

apps.name: bat
apps.text: cat with syntax highlighting and line numbers. Runs a pager for long files.

apps.name: eza
apps.text: A modern ls: colours, file types, trees and long listings.

apps.name: nnn
apps.text: A tiny, fast file manager. Opens files in other programs.

apps.name: ncdu
apps.text: See what takes the space in a directory tree, and clean it up.

apps.name: fzf
apps.text: A fuzzy finder for files, lines and anything else piped into it.

apps.name: Git
apps.text: Version control for repositories on this machine: init, commit, branch, merge, log and diff. Remotes are not served: git's HTTP and SSH helpers have no box of their own and are refused at their installed paths.

apps.name: tig
apps.text: A text interface for browsing a Git repository's history. Runs git.

apps.name: lazygit
apps.text: A terminal interface for Git: stage, commit, branch and rebase with a few keys. Runs git.

apps.name: age
apps.text: Simple, modern file encryption, offline, to a passphrase or to a recipient key made elsewhere. The age-keygen in its package has no box of its own and is refused at its installed path.

apps.name: minisign
apps.text: Sign files and verify signatures, offline, with tiny Ed25519 keys.

apps.name: FLAC
apps.text: Encode and decode lossless FLAC audio files. The metaflac in its package has no box of its own and is refused at its installed path.

apps.name: LAME
apps.text: Encode audio files to MP3.

apps.name: Geth (dev chain)
apps.text: go-ethereum for local development: geth --dev runs a private chain on this machine with its console. It cannot sync a public network here.

apps.name: Profanity (XMPP, OMEMO)
apps.text: A terminal XMPP chat client with OMEMO end-to-end encryption. Every connection leaves over Nym or Anyone, never direct, so your server never learns your address, but it still sees your account, your contacts and when you talk. Its box allows any server: a market release cannot carry a list of servers yet (plan/33, L5).

apps.name: Monero wallet (CLI)
apps.text: Monero's command-line wallet. It starts with a public remote node, xmr-node.cakewallet.com:18081, as an untrusted node, so it offers no mining, and logs to its home; name another with --daemon-address. It reaches the node over Nym or Anyone, never direct, so the node never learns your address; it still sees which outputs your wallet asks about. Its box allows any node: a market release cannot carry a list of destinations yet (plan/33, L5). The daemon and tools in its package have no box of their own and are refused.

apps.name: swayimg
apps.text: An image viewer that opens in its own window: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG and more, with zoom, pan and a slideshow. It reads only files in its own home and has no network at all. It decodes untrusted images with the usual libraries, so a hostile image is held by its box, not by the viewer.

apps.name: Telegram Desktop
apps.text: Telegram's desktop client, in its own window. It reaches Telegram's servers over Anyone, never direct, so they never learn your address. They still see your account's phone number, your contacts, who you talk to and when, and your messages: the desktop app has no secret chats, so nothing it sends is end-to-end encrypted. It runs in its own box, with its own home and no other files.

apps.name: DarkFi wallet (drk)
apps.text: DarkFi's command-line wallet, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0 without its tor and i2p transports, as a prompt in the Terminal: each line runs drk, as wallet --balance or transfer. The first run asks for the wallet's passphrase and makes its first key. Its keys stay in its own home. It asks a darkfid node you name with :node, run elsewhere and reached over Anyone, never direct: the node never learns your address, but it sees which coins your wallet asks about.

apps.name: DarkFi local dev chain
apps.text: A DarkFi chain of your own, for trying the wallet, transfers and contracts: DarkFi's darkfid on its localnet, the minerd that mines its blocks, and the drk prompt, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0, in one box joined on its own loopback. What is mined goes to your wallet. It reaches no network at all, and its coins are worth nothing anywhere else. Its box may JIT, as wasmer does for each contract and RandomX for the proof of work. A home holds a few hours of blocks.

apps.name: DarkIRC (P2P chat)
apps.text: DarkFi's peer-to-peer IRC, in the Terminal: the darkirc daemon, built here from DarkFi v0.5.0 without its tor and i2p transports, with the small IRC client sic beside it in the same box. The first run asks for a nick, and you are joined to DarkFi's channels as the history syncs from peers. Peers are reached over Anyone, never direct, so a peer never learns your address. Peers still see the channels you join and when you talk; encrypted channels hide what is said only from those without the channel key. darkirc listens only on its own box's loopback, for sic.

apps.name: KeePassXC
apps.text: A password manager that keeps your passwords in one encrypted file in its own home, offline. Its box has no network at all, so nothing it holds can leave the machine through it. It opens in its own window in the NØNOS frame; copied passwords go to the NØNOS clipboard, and are cleared there when KeePassXC clears them.

apps.name: foot (terminal)
apps.text: A fast Wayland terminal in its own window, running a shell. Its box may start programs, as a terminal starts its shell, and every program it starts is held to the same box: its own home, no network.

apps.name: mpv (media player)
apps.text: A media player in its own window, for the video and audio files in its own home. It draws in software, with no GPU, and has no network at all, so it plays only what is already in its home. Its box never lets it make code as it runs, so it starts without its Lua scripts: no on-screen controls, keyboard only (space pauses, arrows seek, q quits).

apps.name: SimpleX Chat (terminal)
apps.text: SimpleX Chat v7.0.3 in a terminal: SimpleX's own release binary, not built here, pinned by sha256 and BLAKE3 and checked against SimpleX's signed checksums. It runs in the Debian family's tree with pinned Debian libraries. It reaches SMP servers over Anyone or Nym, never direct, and keeps its database, your profile, contacts and messages, in its own home. That home lasts until the machine powers off: a live session, gone then, until kept homes come.

apps.name: SimpleX Chat core
apps.text: the engine for NØNOS's SimpleX window; not for direct use

apps.name: zathura (PDF viewer)
apps.text: A keyboard-driven PDF viewer that opens in its own window. It opens the documents in its own home, or ones you put there. Its PDF support is the mupdf plugin, zathura-pdf-mupdf, installed with it. It has no network at all, and it runs in its own box, so a hostile PDF is held by that box, not by the viewer.

apps.name: DarkFi (chat app)
apps.text: DarkFi's desktop app, built here from v0.5.0 without tor or i2p. It draws on the CPU, with no GPU, so it is slower than on other systems. Its peers are reached over Anyone, never direct.
